Liudmila Joukovskaya    4:08 AM Hi Daytona team, I saw your ads and I loved simplicity of the setup! I was trying to understand the pricing and I somehow naively thought "surely Daytona must be cheaper than GCP". I am interested in using sandbox for running Codex agents. We do document processing in education space (grading student papers, parsing out examp PDFs), etc. Many of those tasks would run for hours. We currently use GCP VM which codex setup. So I asked gpt-5.5 to give me prices of eg 1

Gautam Talks    4:51 PM Not a feature request, but hopefully useful. I spent a few weeks benchmarking Firecracker guest images and published the harnesses: github.com/GautamTalksDev/mayfly-guest Main finding: most published kernel-stripping advice for Firecracker is stale. Turning ACPI off costs 278ms rather than saving time, because modern Firecracker passes device info through ACPI tables and MPTable booting is now deprecated. Disabling PCI breaks root disk discovery entirely, since CONFIG_PCI

nodes.subtreeText: 3:07 How we support static egress IPs: The recommended approach is to use a VPN connection with Tailscale and route your sandbox traffic through an exit node you control with a known static IP. From your firewall's perspective, all sandbox traffic will originate from that single IP — giving you full control over what to allowlist. This works out of the box in Daytona since Tailscale falls back to TCP when UDP isn't available. Full guide here: daytona.io/docs/en/vpn-connections#…
